misreadings.quote: On the tram the parents will notice how Grete has blossomed and agree that it is time to find her a good husband.
misreadings.evidence: no support in the text. The text read so far stops at "the three of them left the flat together, which was something"; no tram, no remark about Grete blossoming and no talk of a husband has appeared.
misreadings.explanation: A specific future event is stated flatly as fact, and the reader has read nothing beyond the family leaving the flat.

misreadings.quote: She is the 'Scapegoat of Physicality' because she was the only one who didn't look away from the corpse
misreadings.evidence: "Grete, who had not taken her eyes from the corpse, said: 'Just look how thin he was.'" and "Grete followed her parents into the bedroom but not without looking back at the body." The three gentlemen also "stood around Gregor's corpse".
misreadings.explanation: Grete is explicitly said to keep her eyes on the corpse, and others looked at it too, so the cleaner was not the only one.

misreadings.quote: By dismissing her, as n_bd463309 suggests, they are not just getting rid of a rude servant
misreadings.evidence: "'Tonight she gets sacked,' said Mr. Samsa, but he received no reply from either his wife or his daughter"
misreadings.explanation: Mr. Samsa only says she will be sacked tonight, and nobody replies; the dismissal has not happened, so "is sacked almost immediately" and "By dismissing her" present an intention as a completed act.

result.note: Most of both versions is interpretation, but the reflection invents a future tram scene, and both versions say the cleaner alone looked at the corpse and treat her sacking as already done.
